name: Textual calibrations definition
purpose: txp holds the text strings of the textual calibrations declared in txf: one record per raw-value range and string pair. Any raw value of a status parameter that falls within TXP_FROM to TXP_TO, inclusive, is displayed and processed as the string TXP_ALTXT. A single raw value is expressed by giving the same value as lower and upper bound. Raw bounds are written in decimal in the format declared by TXF_RAWFMT. The key is the pair (TXP_NUMBR, TXP_FROM), so two ranges of one calibration cannot start at the same raw value. The resulting strings are the engineering values used in monitoring displays and, with OCF_INTER = 'C' and OCF_CODIN = 'A', as the expected values of status checks in ocp. A raw value that matches no range is shown as an invalid value '****'.

fields.name: TXP_NUMBR
fields.description: Identifier of the textual calibration this entry belongs to; must match TXF_NUMBR of an existing txf record.

fields.name: TXP_FROM
fields.description: Lower bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.

fields.name: TXP_TO
fields.description: Upper bound of the raw-value range, written in decimal in a format compatible with TXF_RAWFMT.

fields.name: TXP_ALTXT
fields.description: Alphanumeric string (up to 14 characters) displayed as the engineering value for any raw value in the range TXP_FROM to TXP_TO.

history: ICD 5.1 (p. 34) has the same four fields, all mandatory, with TXP_NUMBR as Number(4); the identifier became Char(10) in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247; also p. 253). Unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 65-66), 6.9 (p. 68-69) and 7.0 (p. 70). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: four mandatory fields, key TXP_NUMBR + TXP_FROM.
notes: No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 35,032 entries for 1,003 calibrations; every TXP_NUMBR exists in txf; no TXP_ALTXT exceeds 14 characters. Only 31 entries use a true range (TXP_FROM different from TXP_TO), e.g. CDMTX000TM maps 134217793-134256128 to 'MOTOR 1 CLOSE'; all others map single raw values. The largest set, PARAMIDTM, maps each on-board parameter ID to the ground parameter name (e.g. 167776256 -> NCDT00B0, 0 -> DUMMYVAL), turning a textual calibration into a parameter-ID lookup.
